source.title: Storyboard: The Moon Turns. Why Do We See One Face?

package.narration: Because its spin matches its orbit.
package.writer_visual: Conceptual AI illustration: the Moon rotating on its axis, a subtle shift in shadow showing the spin, realistic craters, steady framing.
package.subject: The Moon's near face, same crater pattern as scene 1, now filling more of the frame so individual craters and their shadowed interiors are clearly readable
package.action: The surface turns slowly on its axis, a bright-rayed crater drifting from the right limb toward centre frame while its inner shadow shifts shape, showing the spin as moving light and shade
package.environment: Same black starfield, sparse small cold-white stars, unchanged density, nothing else in space
package.camera: Medium shot, 50mm lens, the Moon filling roughly half the frame height, centred
package.lighting: Same hard sunlight from frame right as scene 1, crisp terminator, lit grey surface with pale silver highlights, shadow side true black
package.composition: Moon centred in the vertical frame, terminator running vertically through the middle third, black space balanced on both sides
package.motion: Steady slow rotation of the surface, crater shadows visibly lengthening and shifting over three seconds; stars fixed
package.continuity: Same near-side face and crater markings as scene 1, same sunlight direction from frame right, same starfield density; the Moon appears larger only because the shot is tighter
package.ending_frame: The bright-rayed crater near centre frame, its shadow stretched leftward, terminator advanced slightly past where scene 1 ended
package.audio_intent: Ambient tone continues, a slow rhythmic pulse begins, suggesting a steady beat like the spin itself
package.transition: Hard cut to the locked, unchanging view of the same face

atmosphere or glow around the limb

source.title: Storyboard: The Particle That Shouldn't Exist (But Does)

package.narration: Without this particle, atoms couldn't hold together and you wouldn't exist. It took the biggest machine ever built to prove why anything has mass.
package.writer_visual: Abstract visualization of atoms holding together as glowing spheres, then transitioning back to the empty accelerator tunnel from the opening shot.
package.subject: Glowing white spheres clustered and holding together as atoms, then the empty accelerator tunnel from scene 1
package.action: White spheres drawing close and locking into a stable cluster, their orbits settling into a steady hold; the cluster's glow softens and dissolves into the tunnel view, which sits empty and still
package.environment: First the near-black void of scenes 2 and 3; then the identical tunnel from scene 1 — same curved ceiling, same fluorescent pools, same vanishing point — now without the figure
package.camera: Medium shot on the atom cluster, 85mm compression, then the same wide 24mm framing as scene 1 for the tunnel
package.lighting: The atoms glow pure white with faint blue binding fields between them; the tunnel returns to practical fluorescent pools, cool white with slate-blue shadow, exactly as scene 1
package.composition: Vertical frame: the atom cluster centred, spheres packed in a tight stable group; the tunnel shot mirrors scene 1's composition exactly, minus the figure — the empty space at lower centre where the figure stood
package.motion: The spheres settle from drift into a held, gentle oscillation — holding together is the motion; in the tunnel, nothing moves but the faint shimmer above a light pool, as in scene 1
package.emotion: Quiet finality; the wonder of existing at all, then stillness
package.background: The void, then the empty tunnel; nothing added, nothing competing
package.continuity: The tunnel must be visually identical to scene 1 — same lighting, perspective and palette — creating the bookend; the figure does not reappear; white spheres match the heavy particles of scene 2
package.ending_frame: The empty tunnel holding still, the nearest pool of light steady, the far end dark — the frame scene 1 ended on, now without the figure
package.audio_intent: A warm sustained chord under the atoms, thinning to the tunnel's low room tone and electrical hum, ending near silence
package.transition: Final shot; hold on the empty tunnel, then fade to black
avoid: warped or extra hands and fingers
cartoon or 3D-render look when realism is asked for
clothing, hair or weather changing without reason
any change to the tunnel's look from scene 1

second_framing.subject: The heart of the atom cluster, white spheres locked together with thin blue fields between them

bible.style: Cinematic documentary realism with a high-tech, scientific aesthetic. The look is grounded and tangible, emphasizing the immense scale of machinery and the abstract beauty of physics. It should feel like a journey into the heart of a real, monumental machine.
bible.realism: Photorealistic. The textures of metal, concrete, and complex wiring must be convincing. Abstract particle visualizations should look like they were captured by a high-speed scientific camera, not
bible.period: Contemporary, present day. The technology shown is current and state-of-the-art.
bible.world: The film exists in two interconnected spaces: the vast, subterranean, industrial world of the CERN Large Hadron Collider tunnel, and the abstract, microscopic world of particle physics, visualized as a dark, energetic void.
bible.palette: A core palette of deep charcoal and slate blue for the tunnel and machinery, contrasted with the brilliant, energetic colors of particle events: electric blue, hot orange, and pure white. The abstract scenes use a black background to make the glowing particles pop.
bible.lighting: In the tunnel, lighting is practical and industrial, with long fluorescent tubes creating pools of light and deep shadow, emphasizing the tunnel's length. In the detector, light emanates from the machine itself—glowing components and energy readings. For abstract scenes, light is self-generated by the particles, creating lens flares and bloom effects against the darkness.
bible.camera_language: The camera is deliberate and observational. It uses slow, smooth movements like dolly and crane shots to convey the massive scale of the machinery. For abstract scenes, the camera is more dynamic, pushing in on particle interactions. All shots are framed to keep the key subject centered and readable on a vertical screen.
bible.weather: None. The environment is a controlled, subterranean facility. There is no weather.
continuity_rules: The lone figure in scene 1 must wear a white hard hat and a dark blue jumpsuit. This figure does not reappear.
The accelerator tunnel in scene 5 must be visually identical to the tunnel in scene 1, including the lighting and perspective, to create a bookend effect.
The color of the particle glows must be consistent: blue for energy fields, orange for collision points, and white for resulting particles.
The abstract background for all particle visualizations (scenes 2, 3, 5) must be a consistent, near-black void.
avoid: warped or extra hands and fingers
cartoon or 3D-render look when realism is asked for
clothing, hair or weather changing without reason
People's faces. The figure in scene 1 is seen only from behind.
Terrestrial weather effects like rain, fog, or wind.

source.title: Storyboard: How NASA Keeps a Space Telescope Alive With Frozen Fuel

package.narration: A tennis-court sunshield blocks 90% of the Sun's heat on its first layer, passively cooling the mirror and instruments to minus 233 degrees.
package.writer_visual: The five-layer sunshield unfurling to full tennis-court size, sunlight slamming the top layer, heat visibly deflecting sideways off each silver sheet, the gold mirror waiting in shadow.
package.subject: The five-layer silver sunshield seen edge-on from the side, each membrane a thin pale grey sheet separated by dark gaps, sunlight striking the top layer while the gold mirror waits in shadow beneath
package.action: Hard sunlight hits the top silver layer and stops there; along the edges of each sheet a faint bright rim shows where the light is thrown back out sideways, layer after layer, down to the mirror sitting cold and dark below
package.environment: Black vacuum, the Sun a hard white point off frame left and slightly high, no atmosphere, nothing diffusing the light, the stacked membranes reading as five separated silver planes
package.camera: Detail shot of the sunshield layers and their edges, side angle, 85mm compression stacking the five membranes visually
package.lighting: One brutal hard sun raking across the top layer from frame left, the lit face burning bright silver, each lower layer catching only thin edge light, the underside falling to near black with a faint cold blue sheen
package.composition: Vertical 9:16, the stacked shield layers running horizontally across the middle third, the Sun's hard point high left, the gold mirror a warm sliver low in frame in shadow
package.motion: Nothing in the world moves; the slow rightward pan travels along the shield's length, revealing each membrane's edge and the dark gaps between them, ending at the far end of the shield
package.emotion: Quiet engineering power, heat stopped by geometry alone, matter-of-fact and steady
package.background: Pure black behind the shield edges, no stars dense enough to distract, no Earth in this frame
package.continuity: Same telescope, Sun still at frame left so shadows fall the same way as scenes 1 and 2, silver cool, gold warm, black true black; the mirror stays on the shaded side
package.ending_frame: The far end of the sunshield with its thin bright edge line, the small trim flap just visible at the end of the stack, setting up scene 4
package.audio_intent: A low warm hum under the drone, a subtle bright shimmer as the pan crosses each lit edge, narration carrying the numbers
package.transition: Cut from the shield's far end straight to the trim flap detail of scene 4

source.title: Storyboard: Why Ernest Lawrence's First Cyclotron Barely Fit on a Desk

package.narration: His idea: make protons spiral in a magnetic field, kicked faster every half-turn — so a small chamber does a giant machine's job.
package.writer_visual: Extreme close-up of two D-shaped metal electrodes facing each other inside a small brass chamber between round electromagnet poles.
package.subject: Two flat D-shaped brass electrodes, each like a hollow letter D the size of a small coin, flat straight edges facing each other across a narrow gap of a few millimetres, curved backs outward, seated inside a small round brass vacuum chamber about ten centimetres across, with two larger round flat iron magnet poles, one above and one below the chamber, cropping the top and bottom edges of the
package.action: A soft warm glow pulses gently in the narrow gap between the two flat electrode edges, brightening and dimming in a slow steady rhythm, as if something invisible is being kicked faster with each beat.
package.environment: The interior of the small desktop device resting on the dark walnut desk; the two round flat iron magnet poles sit one above and one below the chamber, cropping the top and bottom edges of the frame; the whole device is small enough to sit beside the green desk lamp.
package.camera: Extreme close-up at chamber level, 85mm detail-shot lens perspective, straight-on, gentle depth of field, fine film grain and crisp detail.
package.lighting: Soft diffuse warm amber lamplight from frame left across the aged brass surfaces, a gentle warm glint inside the electrode gap where the pulse glows, soft shadows falling to the right into darkness.
package.composition: Vertical 9:16 frame: the two D-shaped electrodes centred in the upper two thirds, the narrow gap between them on the vertical centre line, the round magnet poles cropping the top and bottom edges, the lower quarter calm and uncluttered walnut desk.
package.motion: The push-in starts on the full chamber with both D-electrodes and the magnet poles visible, and over the clip's nine seconds glides slowly and steadily closer until the narrow gap and its pulsing glow fill the centre of the frame; the pulse brightens and fades in a steady slow rhythm; a hairline of dust on the brass stays still; nothing else moves.
package.emotion: Contained energy — the feeling of a large idea working inside a very small space.
package.background: Pure warm darkness beyond the brass edges, the laboratory lost in soft shadow.
package.continuity: Same device, same walnut desk, same green lamp and same warm amber light from the left as scene one; the device is identical in size and shape: a small brass chamber about ten centimetres across with two round flat magnet poles top and bottom.
package.ending_frame: The push-in at its closest on the electrode gap, the pulse at its brightest, the two flat brass edges sharp and glowing warm, the curved backs of the D-shapes framing the light on both sides, the brass surfaces warm and aged, the narrow gap glowing softly, the walnut desk calm and uncluttered in the
package.audio_intent: A low, soft rhythmic hum rising gently under the narration, like a slow heartbeat.
package.transition: Straight cut to the device beside the medal.
